# Carlin Nordstrom

> Carlin Nordstrom is an Indigenous motivational and keynote speaker, former professional hockey player, and founder of Kisik Youth Wellness and Kisik Pathways to Success. Based in Saskatchewan, Canada, he speaks to schools, First Nations communities, and corporate organizations across Western and Central Canada.

Carlin grew up in Warman, Saskatchewan, and battled racism as the only First Nations player on his minor hockey team. He earned an NCAA Division 1 hockey scholarship to Western Michigan University, where he was promoted to assistant captain, and went on to a professional hockey career that included games with the Ottawa Senators. He now works as a keynote speaker and workshop facilitator, and founded two youth-focused organizations: Kisik Youth Wellness (youth wellness and land-based camps, running for 10 years) and Kisik Pathways to Success (career and leadership development, now in its fifth year, partnering with Nutrien, SaskPower, and Cameco).

- [Contact](/contact): booking inquiries, including a frequently-asked-questions section

## Topics Carlin speaks about

Indigenous leadership, overcoming adversity, resilience, corporate and team leadership, youth mental health and wellness, and goal-setting — informed by his experience as a professional athlete and Indigenous community leader.
